steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Fate (fatum) is the driving force of the Aeneid: Aeneas's destiny to found Rome is decreed by Jupiter and cannot be avoided. | Key Fact: Pietas (duty to gods, country, and family) is Aeneas's defining quality: he is called 'pius Aeneas' throughout the epic. But pietas demands terrible personal sacrifices. | Key Fact: Love and loss: Dido's love for Aeneas and her suicide is the Aeneid's most tragic episode, showing how fate destroys personal happiness. | Key Fact: Power and transformation in Ovid: the gods use power to pursue desire, and transformation is both punishment and escape.
